widget.instructions: The board shows the forces on the body; press Play to see its motion.

stem: A {{m}} kg box slides {{d}} m along a level floor.
How much work does the floor's normal force do on the box?

options.text: A negative amount, because it pushes up while the box moves along

hints.text: Work counts only the part of a force along the displacement.
The box moves horizontally; the normal force points straight up.
W = F d cos θ with θ = 90°.

perpendicular-force-does-work.text: The normal force is vertical and the displacement is horizontal: cos 90° = 0, so it does no work.

generic.text: A force perpendicular to the displacement does no work.

workedSolution.text: The normal force is at 90° to the displacement.

perpendicular-force-does-work.front: Does the normal force do work on a box sliding along a level floor?
perpendicular-force-does-work.back: No: it is perpendicular to the displacement, so W = F d cos 90° = 0.

generic.front: Work by a force perpendicular to the motion?

accessibility.altText: A box on a floor with its weight and the normal force drawn.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Choose an answer with the radio buttons.
